question: For a ticket whose build touches ONLY proofs/validations (no source), what satisfies the hollow rung at PROVED — (A) hollow_lacks treats a reading whose every skipped file is a proof/validation as not-applicable (the ticket is proved by the proof's own red-before/green-after, recorded on the seal), (B) the tester's --hollow reverts the PROOF for such tickets and records the pre-fix red as the reading, or (C) something else you have in mind?
why_it_blocks: 9c46e187f2de is a bug ticket whose whole build is the proof file (test_chart_tree.py) plus its validation; the door it exercises was untouched by design. cairn test --hollow skips both writes_to files by construction (a proof is the instrument, a validation is a record) and lands evidence.hollow[9c46e187f2de] = {} — and clearance.hollow_lacks reds an empty reading as [hollow_nothing_measured] (the cf80bdb57205 rule, 2026-09-15), so PROVED will refuse. The rule's FIX line ('make the decompose berth name repo files the build writes') cannot apply: the build wrote no source on purpose. Only concept-piece is exempt from the hollow rung today. The proof is sealed green (2026-09-17T19:55:52) and reads red against its own pre-fix bytes (commit c388c386), which is the evidence a proof-only fix can have.
